headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.8340). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 12 studies yielded an effect size of 0.98 (95% CI: 0.76–1.26), indicating no statistically significant association between beta-carotene and prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 75.98%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
